key_insight: GaitFM transfers knowledge from large vision models to wearable sensor data to improve gait assessment across tasks and sensor setups.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more accessible assessment of gait changes associated with neurological and musculoskeletal conditions.
method: Transfer visual knowledge to a cross-modal model for inertial measurement unit (IMU) signals.
Pretrain on unlabeled gait data from diverse conditions, sensor modalities, and body locations.
Evaluate gait parameter estimation, disease and abnormality detection, and clinical outcome prediction.
evidence_signal: Pretraining included about 4,000 participants and 1.23 million gait windows; the abstract reports strong performance across 18 tasks and generalization across sensor configurations and body locations.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance estimates or prospective clinical validation, leaving real-world reliability uncertain.
paper_title: GaitFM: A Cross-Modal Foundation Model for Wearable Gait Assessment
